boards.title: Your First Weekend at California State University-San Bernardino, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A flexible Friday-to-Sunday introduction to CSUSB, combining practical campus orientation, recreation, art, student-life spaces, and a conditional public stargazing finale.

cards.title: Start with a Campus Landmark
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Legacy Fountain
cards.notes: Begin at the fountain near the Physical Education Building, then use the surrounding paths to learn the campus layout.
cards.short_summary: An easy outdoor starting point anchored by a documented CSUSB landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSB identifies Legacy Fountain as a campus landmark unveiled during its 50th-anniversary festivities on September 20, 2015.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; ordinary campus access conditions apply.

cards.title: Learn the Library’s First Floor
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · John M. Pfau Library
cards.notes: Find the service desk, research-help point, course reserves, and Makerspace now so the building feels familiar later.
cards.short_summary: A practical first pass through the library services students commonly need.
cards.evidence_claim: Pfau Library’s first floor contains its service desk, course reserves, research assistance, Makerspace, and Interlibrary Loan office.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current hours page before visiting; some services require a Coyote OneCard.

cards.entity_name: Robert and Frances Fullerton Museum of Art
cards.title: Add an Art-Museum Hour
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · RAFFMA
cards.notes: Walk through the current galleries, then ask about the Egyptian collection if you want to arrange a separate appointment.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission museum stop with rotating exhibitions and Egyptian antiquities.
cards.evidence_claim: RAFFMA states that admission is free for all visitors and that its Journey to the Beyond Egyptian Gallery currently requires an appointment.
cards.access_notes: Public hours are listed as Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; verify gallery status before going.

cards.title: Map the Student-Life Hub
cards.subtitle: Friday late afternoon · SMSU North
cards.notes: Tour all three floors, noting the bookstore, food choices, bowling area, student offices, and third-floor affinity centers.
cards.short_summary: A quick orientation to a major cluster of food, activities, and student support.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSB describes SMSU North as a three-story facility containing eateries, Coyote Lanes, the Coyote Bookstore, affinity centers, club offices, and leadership programs.
cards.access_notes: Individual businesses and activity areas may keep hours different from the building.

cards.title: Choose a Low-Pressure Dinner Stop
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Coyote Commons
cards.notes: Use the dining hall as a natural group meetup; confirm the current service schedule and your meal-plan access before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A campus dining stop that gives the first evening a simple gathering point.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSB identifies Coyote Commons as the campus dining hall serving students, staff, and faculty.
cards.source_title: CSUSB Department of Housing and Residential Education to Offer Tours of New Coyote Village
cards.access_notes: Confirm current dining hours and accepted meal-plan or payment options; service varies by term.

cards.entity_name: Santos Manuel Student Union South Clock Tower
cards.title: Listen for the Coyote Howl
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · SMSU South Clock Tower
cards.notes: Look up at the clock tower while crossing SMSU South; return at noon Tuesday or Thursday to hear the documented howl.
cards.short_summary: A first-weekend preview of a recurring, school-specific sound tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSB documents that the SMSU South clock tower plays a Coyote Howl every Tuesday and Thursday at noon as a campus tradition.
cards.access_notes: The tower can be viewed during ordinary campus access; the documented howl occurs Tuesday and Thursday at noon.

cards.title: Queue Up a Friendly Game
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Esports Arena, SMSU South 117
cards.notes: Bring your student identification, choose a PC or Nintendo Switch title, and use the session to meet other campus gamers.
cards.short_summary: A student-only gaming stop with equipment provided at no additional charge.
cards.evidence_claim: The CSUSB Esports Arena has 18 gaming PCs and two Nintendo Switch consoles that are free for CSUSB students to use.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Monday–Thursday 11 a.m.–8 p.m. and Friday 11 a.m.–5 p.m.; guests must accompany a student.

cards.title: Try One Recreation Feature
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Student Recreation & Wellness Center
cards.notes: Pick one manageable activity—fitness floor, indoor court, bouldering, or an outdoor court—and review access rules first.
cards.short_summary: A structured Saturday start with several indoor and outdoor activity choices.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSB lists a fitness floor, indoor court, climbing and bouldering wall, studios, tennis courts, basketball courts, fields, and sand volleyball at the center.
cards.access_notes: Current summer weekend hours are listed as 8 a.m.–3 p.m.; enrolled-student access is included in tuition.

cards.title: Locate the Coyotes’ Home Court
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Coussoulis Arena
cards.notes: Walk around the arena exterior and note the nearby athletic fields; enter only for a scheduled event with valid access.
cards.short_summary: A daylight orientation stop connecting the arena with CSUSB’s athletic grounds.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUSB identifies Coussoulis Arena as the home of its volleyball and basketball teams and notes nearby softball, soccer, and cross-country fields.
cards.access_notes: Exterior orientation is flexible; interior entry depends on the event schedule, ticketing, and venue rules.

cards.title: Use Stargazing as the Optional Finale
cards.subtitle: Saturday night when scheduled · Murillo Family Observatory
cards.notes: Check for an announced Visitor Night, confirm weather and admission details, and skip the hilltop trip if no opening is posted.
cards.short_summary: A conditional night-sky finale tied to the observatory’s recurring public program.
cards.evidence_claim: The Murillo Family Observatory is a research facility that hosts public Visitor Nights during the academic year, weather permitting, and otherwise is not open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Visit only for a posted Visitor Night; timing, weather, admission, and parking requirements must be confirmed for that event.

warnings: The observatory finale is conditional because public access is limited to announced Visitor Nights and depends on weather.
Campus dining, recreation, library, arena, museum, and student-union schedules can change between academic terms; verify same-day access.
